full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioners is that a Hat named Baluchar Hat was running within Mouza Baluchar, PS Shirajdikhan, District Munshiganj. The land of the said Hat was submerged in the process of erosion and was engulfed by Dhaleswari river in 1396 BS. The Hat-going people with theactive support of the then Upazila Administration started a Bazar in the nearby land belonging to the petitioners without their consent. However, the said Hat was running well in the name of Baluchar Munshir Hat. Nter expiry of 1396 BS the owners of the land approaced the Government for setting up of the Bazar under the East-Pakistan Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Acquisition) Ordinance, 1959 as amended. Thereafter, the Government issued licence to the owners of the land including the petitioners permitting them to continue with the Bazar vide Memo No.5/4/Rajasha/l1.6.89 dated 4.4.90 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Munshiganj for the year 1397 BS. Thereafter, the licence was renewed for 1398 BS. Thereafter, for renewal of licence for the year 1399 BS a sum or Taka 44,250.00 was demanded and it was mentioned in the demand note that it was for a temporary period and that the licensees would be bound by any future allotment for the Hat Bazar as may be made by the Government. The licensees did not deposit the renewal fee and made representation to the Government for waiving the condition attached to the renewal order (Annexure-D) and requested the authority concerned to renew the licence in the name of Baluchar Munshir Hat Bazar as before. Thereafter, the District Administration directed the licensees to deposit the renewal fee for a period of 5 months from Baisak to Bhadra, 1399 BS with intimation that proposal for naming the Hat after individual name has been rejected. Against the said order, the petitioners preferred an appeal before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division under section 147 of the East Bengal Estate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The said appeal was registered as Appeal No. 103 of 1992 and it was admitted and the records were called for and during pendency of the appeal the operation of the impugned order was stayed. The petitioners were informed by some of the shopkeepers that they were asked to remove their shops with structures to a nearby land wherein a Hat has been established in the name of Baluchar Hat. The petitioners after enquiry came to know that the Ministry of Land vacated the order of stay granted by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division by the impugned order and the Thana Administration has received instructions to demolish the Baluchar Munshir Hat and letters were issued to the shop keepers. The petitioners also came to learn that on an application filed by one Bani Amin, President of Bahichar Hat Bazar Development Committee, the Ministry of Land passed the order directing the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka to send the case record of the said appeal to that Ministry if it could not be disposed of within 11.11.93 No notice was issued to the petitioners when the records were called for nor when the order of stay was vacated. 

 5. It is the further case of the said respondents that the Hat is known as Baluchar Hat and it was recognised as such by the Government and that Appeal No. 103 of 1992 was not maintainable as the order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Munshiganj was not passed under any provision of Part- V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but it was passed under section 2 of the Hats and Bazars (Establishment and Acquisition) Ordinance, 1959. The Ministry of Land had jurisdiction to call for the records and vacate the order of stay granted in the appeal and that the impugned order was passed with lawful authority. The Baluchar Hat was established and was under the management of the Government since 1975 and it was completely submerged and a temporary hat was set up on 1.90 acres of hired land. Thereafter, some persons gifted 1.90 acres of land in favour of the Government and in that land the Baluchar Hat has been re-established and, as such, the temporary licences of the owners including the petitioners were cancelled. The petitioners filed a writ petition against the establishment of the Baluchar Hat newly which was summarily rejected. The half portion of the Hat for which temporary licences were issued had been submerged under water and majority of the owners gifted the land situated in nearby place where the Baluchar Hat has been established. So, the present writ petition is not maintainable. 

 9. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Additional Attorney General, appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 4, submitted that no appeal lies against any order passed under section 2 of the Hats and Bazars (Establishment and Acquisition) Ordinance, 1959 and that East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has no application to the present case and as such the Government has the right to withdraw the appeal and passed necessary orders. He also submitted that under the Rules of Business of the Government, the Divisional Commissioner is under the supervision of the Ministry and the Ministry may pass any order in respect of a matter pending before the Divisional Commissioner or Additional Divisional Commissioner or to call for the records from their office in administrative capacity. As the pending appeal was incompetent, the admission of the same and passing the order of stay was unlawful and as such the impugned order cannot be saic to have been passed without lawful authority. He nezt submitted that in any view of the matter, the impugned order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue)  Munshiganj refusing to grant licence for 1399 BS was not in force after Chaitra, 1399 BS and. as such, the appeal' has in the meantime become infructuous and consequently this Rule also has become infructuous. He also submitted that the petitioners have no right to establish any Hat under the name of Baluchar Munshirhat which was originally Baluchar Hat After the previous Baluchar Hat was submerged and the said Baluchar Hat was re-established, there is no existence of Baluchar Munshirhat and this Baluchar Munshirhat was never recognised by the Government in accordance with law and, as such, the order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) which was impugned before the Additional Divisional Commissioner also has no substance. He also cited various decisions in support of his submissions. 

 14. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Additional Attorney-General, has drawn our attention to various provisions of Hats and Bazar Regulations and State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and also some decisions showing, prima facie. that the appeal is not maintainable. 

 17. From Annexures A and B to the petition of the instant case it appears that an order was passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Munshiganj granting licence to the petitioners for 1397 BS and accordingly, the licence was granted under section 2(3) of the Hats and Bazars (Establishment and Acquisition) Ordinance, 1959 for one year. So, the present case is also more or less similar to the reported case. Whether the petitioners will be granted licence or not or will be allowed to continue the market or not the law will take its own course but the appeal pending before the Additional Divisional Commissioner cannot be said to be infructuous after expiry of 1399 BS and consequently, this writ petition has also not become infructuous.
